main_argument_chains.claim: The improved epidemic model is used to convert outbreak dynamics into intervention quantities and policy thresholds.
support_steps: Fit SEIR baseline to reported curves.
Add hospital, corpse, and contact-tracing mechanisms.
Compare calculated and reported cumulative cases.
Compute medicine demand and weighted delivery centers.
Vary capacity, efficacy, and contact tracing.
Translate outputs into a bounded recommendation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the result as a conditional intervention-planning framework requiring joint uncertainty and external operational validation.

main_argument_chains.claim: The article's strongest reusable move is the handoff from a fitted dynamic model to an operational allocation and then to a decision threshold.
support_steps: CUM is defined as a model output.
Demand is derived from CUM and growth.
Capacity and efficacy alter intervention scenarios.
Control and eradication are defined mathematically.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep model-to-decision interfaces explicit in future Problem A papers.
